rounds.fact: Zillow launched in 2006 and was one of the first sites to give the public free access to home value estimates, a feature ('Zestimate') that unsettled a lot of real estate agents at the time.
Delicious (originally styled del.icio.us) popularized social bookmarking and the very concept of a 'tag,' letting users save and label links for themselves and everyone else to browse.
Yelp started in 2004 as an email-based referral service before pivoting to the review-website format it's known for today, after users kept asking for a public place to post reviews.
Star ratings lasted until 2010. They were retired because almost everyone rated either 5 stars or 1, so the site switched to thumbs up/down.
StumbleUpon's whole concept was a browser button that took you to a random, algorithm-picked website matching your interests, a discovery model that faded as social feeds took over that role.
